slides.0.points.0.label: Organic farming
slides.0.points.0.text: Synthetic pesticides and fertilisers prohibited, EU certified; Portugal has 3,500+ hectares of organic vineyards
slides.0.points.1.label: Biodynamic farming
slides.0.points.1.text: Work follows lunar phases and cosmic rhythms, Demeter certified, with a deeper philosophical dimension
slides.0.points.2.label: Natural wine
slides.0.points.2.text: Minimal-intervention winemaking, no filtration or fining, no added SO₂, with highly varied and extreme styles
slides.1.title: Core Differences Between the Three Approaches
slides.1.html:
Item Organic farming Biodynamic farming Natural wine
Certification body EU Organic / Ecocert Demeter / Biodyvin No official certification (associations such as AVN)
Pesticides Synthetic pesticides banned; copper and sulphur allowed As organic, plus biodynamic preparations Usually organic or biodynamic as a base
Winemaking intervention No particular restrictions Tends towards minimal intervention Strictest: no added yeast, very low SO₂
Lunar phases/cosmos Not required Core principle Referenced by some practitioners
Stylistic consistency High Medium-high Low (varies greatly each year)
slides.2.title: Pioneering Natural Wine Producers in Portugal
slides.2.items.0.desc: Dirk Niepoort: whole-cluster fermentation and minimal SO₂; Batuta and Charme are benchmarks of the natural wine world
slides.2.items.1.desc: Biodynamic farming; Álvaro Castro's old-vine Touriga Nacional, with pure minerality
slides.2.items.2.desc: Organic farming; a modern interpretation of Baga, rich yet refined, breaking Bairrada's traditional image of harsh astringency
slides.2.items.3.desc: Organic farming; tiny-batch single-variety Madeira showing fine terroir detail
slides.3.question: Which description of natural wine is the most accurate?
slides.3.options.0: It has official EU certification, equivalent to organic certification
slides.3.options.2: It has no unified official certification; the core idea is minimal-intervention winemaking with very little or no added SO₂
slides.3.options.3: It must be a sparkling style (Pétillant Naturel)
slides.3.explanation: Natural wine currently has no globally unified official certification standard; associations in different places (such as AVN in France and VinNatur in Italy) set their own. The core idea is organic/biodynamic farming in the vineyard plus minimal intervention in the cellar, usually with no or very little added sulphur dioxide (SO₂).
slides.4.message: Congratulations on completing the natural wine lesson!
